memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'When a woman has her regular flow of blood, the impurity of her monthly period will last seven days, and anyone who touches her will be unclean till evening.'" - Lev 15:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Seven days, every month, for most of her adult life. That is a significant portion of a woman's years spent ceremonially unclean.

We must be careful how we read this. It does not mean God found women shameful, or that menstruation was a sin. It was the loss of blood — and blood, throughout Leviticus, is life. The life of a creature is in the blood (Lev 17:11). Wherever life drained away, cleansing was required before approaching the living God.

But we should also be honest that this was costly for women in a way it was not for men, and Scripture does not explain why the burden fell as it did.

What we can say with certainty is how Jesus treated women who lived under these laws. He did not keep His distance. When a woman who had bled for twelve years — twelve years of continuous uncleanness, twelve years without normal touch — reached out and took hold of His cloak in a crowd, He did not recoil. He stopped everything, found her, and called her Daughter (Mark 5:34).

Daughter. To a woman the law had kept at arm's length for over a decade.

That is the heart of God towards every woman reading this chapter.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you ever felt that your body puts you at a distance from God?
2. What does Jesus calling her "Daughter" say to you?
3. How does Christ's treatment of women shape your understanding of God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You did not turn away from the woman everyone else avoided, but called her Daughter. Let me hear Your welcome over my own life. Amen.
